description: Reference composed experience: why the Moon has phases.

variables.label: Moon's position in its orbit
variables.description: Drag the Moon around Earth. 0° is between Earth and the Sun (new moon); 180° is opposite the Sun (full moon).

content.title: Why the Moon has phases
content.explanation: The Moon does not make its own light. Half of it is always lit by the Sun. As the Moon orbits Earth, we see that lit half from different angles: the lit part we can see grows from new moon to full moon and shrinks back again.
tryThis: Drag the orbit slider to the far side of Earth, opposite the Sun. Which half of the Moon is lit, and can you see it from Earth?
Set the slider halfway. About half the Moon appears lit - that is a quarter moon. Read the illuminated fraction.
Test the idea that Earth's shadow causes phases: watch the Moon pass behind Earth at full moon. Does its lit fraction change on this orbit, far from the shadow?
Find the slider position where the illuminated fraction is 0. Where is the Moon relative to the Sun?
content.keyIdea: Phases come from seeing different parts of the Moon's always-lit half as it orbits Earth - not from Earth's shadow.
